subject: Combining accelerator credits with onboarding discount — packaging question
messages:
From: Olly Carter <olly@sproutlabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@sproutlabs.com>, procurement@sproutlabs.com
Date: 2026-08-10T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Packaging question: combine accelerator credits with onboarding discount?

Hi Vanessa,

Quick question from our side as we finalize the supplier shortlist for our fall cohort. Sprout Labs qualified for an accelerator credit pool with you (60k tokens equivalent) but we also like the onboarding discount you mentioned in the pitch (15% off committed Dedicated for first 3 months).

Is there a standard way to blend those two incentives? Specifically:
- Can a portion of the accelerator credits be converted to a one-time onboarding discount applied to a Dedicated commitment?
- If conversion is allowed, what is the approval path and timeline (legal/procurement signoff)?
- Any restrictions on using promo credits for reserved capacity purchases versus hosted usage?

Procurement will need a short summary for their approval thread. Happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

Thanks,
Olly
Olly Carter

Sprout Labs

Subject: Re: Packaging question: combine accelerator credits with onboarding discount?

Hi Olly,

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: we can structure a compromise but it is case-by-case. Looping Ben (pricing) and Lauren (legal/ops) to propose a concrete path.

From a process perspective:
- We typically do not apply promo credits directly as percent discounts on Dedicated commitments because accounting needs to treat them as contra-revenue.
- We can offer a convertible path: a portion of the accelerator credits can be converted to an equivalent monetary credit that is applied to the first invoice of a Dedicated commitment. This requires approvals from Pricing and Finance and a simple SOW amendment.
- Conversion rules we usually see: credits convert at list unit price, expire 90 days from conversion, and cannot be used for third-party cloud charges.

Ben and Lauren, can you propose a model with numbers that we can share with Sprout Procurement? Olly, can you confirm the target committed qps/size if you convert to Dedicated so we can size the discount?

Happy to put together a 1-page and a draft SOW amendment.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-11T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question: combine accelerator credits with onboarding discount?

Hi all,

Thanks Vanessa. Proposed compromise below (numbers are illustrative — happy to refine):

Proposal
- Accelerator pool: 60k credits (token equivalent). We agree to allow conversion of up to 40% of that pool (24k credits) into a monetary onboarding credit.
- Conversion rate: 1 credit = $0.12 (list unit rate for hosted generation). 24k credits -> $2,880 onboarding credit.
- Onboarding application: top-line credit applied to first Dedicated invoice after signing a 3-month minimum Dedicated commitment at Standard tier.
- Expiration: converted credit expires 90 days after DocuSign completion.
- Usage restrictions: converted credit covers Redwood invoice charges only; cannot be used to offset cloud infra pass-through or taxes.

Operational steps
1) Customer signs an amendment (SOW) documenting conversion amount and commitment term.
2) Legal approves amendment; Finance issues a billing note.
3) DocuSign link issued and procurement can sign.

Pros/cons
- Pros: gives Sprout a meaningful onboarding headstart without us giving open-ended percent discounts.
- Cons: small administrative overhead and requires Finance acceptance.

I attached a short spreadsheet with worked examples at different conversion levels and a draft SOW template.

Ben

Pricing Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben, Vanessa — this looks workable. A few quick clarifications from our procurement lead:

- Can we get the converted credit window extended to 120 days instead of 90? Our internal billing cycle may delay first invoice.
- We need a brief statement that the converted credit does not constitute a recurring discount and will only apply once. Procurement also wants a clear invoice line item describing the credit.
- Any SLA implications? We may want a 99.9% uptime target for the Dedicated trial period; if you have an SLA addendum we can attach that to the SOW.

If those are acceptable, I think procurement will sign quickly. I can share the procurement contact and their standard PO template.

Olly
Olly Carter
Head of Platform Partnerships, Sprout Labs

Hi Olly,

Thanks — we can accommodate the slight tweaks. Final agreed terms below for signature:

Agreed terms summary
- Conversion amount: 24,000 accelerator credits converted to a one-time onboarding credit (equivalent $2,880 at list rate).
- Commitment: Sprout signs a 3-month Dedicated commitment (Standard tier) with expected baseline throughput of ~20 qps.
- Redemption window: Converted credit valid for 120 days after DocuSign signature.
- Expiration and usage: Single-use credit applied to Redwood invoice line item titled 'Onboarding conversion credit - SPR-2026-1294'. Not applicable to cloud pass-throughs or taxes.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime SLA applies to Dedicated environment for the first 90 days; extended SLA remedies described in SOW appendix A.

Next steps
1) I attached a draft SOW amendment for your review (SOW-sprout-draft.pdf).
2) Ben/Finance will confirm billing flow and invoice line item.
3) I will send a DocuSign link once legal confirms the amendment language.

If procurement confirms PO template, Lauren will coordinate the DocuSign. Looking forward to getting Sprout onboarded.

Best,
